title: us-health-appeal-rules
description: Machine-readable rules for appealing a health insurance denial in the United States: deadlines, protections, rights and process steps, each with a legal reference, a primary source and a last-verified date. A rule file (rules/*.json) is a RuleFile; help-resources.json is a HelpResourceFile.

Jurisdiction.description: "federal" (ACA/ERISA baseline), "nsa" (No Surprises Act) or a state code. Must match the file name: federal.json, nsa.json, tx.json.

RuleCategory.description: deadline = a clock; protection = a limit on what can be billed or denied; right = something the person may request; process = what the plan or regulator must do, by when.

AppliesIf.description: Conditions, ANDed. An omitted key matches anything. {} means the rule always applies within its jurisdiction.

self_funded.description: "no" = insured plans only (state law reaches them; self-funded ERISA plans are federal-only). "yes" = self-funded only. "any" = regardless. Consumers who do not know their funding should still be shown "no" rules, with the caveat.

anchor.description: The date the statute counts from. The consumer supplies it.

unit.description: Keep the statute's own unit; do not convert months to days.

who.description: consumer = a countdown for the person; insurer = the plan's clock, informational.

id.description: Stable identifier jurisdiction.topic.detail (fed.*, nsa.*, tx.*). Never reused after removal.

title.description: Starts with the jurisdiction name, states the fact, about 12 words.

summary.description: Plain English, Grade 8, 60 words or fewer, no advice language. Safe to show or speak to a consumer.

legal_ref.description: Statute or regulation section as a lawyer cites it.

source_url.description: The primary source a human read: eCFR, the legislature or the regulator.

last_verified.description: The date a human read source_url. Rules older than 45 days fail validate.mjs.

priority.description: Display order within a jurisdiction, lower first. No Surprises Act rules use 1-6; state rules start at 10.

why_template.description: One sentence explaining why this applies, true whether or not plan funding is known.

caveat.description: Shown when the rule is displayed under uncertainty (e.g. unknown plan funding).

scope.description: "federal" entries are the fallback for states without their own.

phone.description: As printed on the source page.

what_they_do.description: One or two sentences: what a caller can expect.
